messages:
eve_support: Heads-up: Ledgex is seeing sustained 429s on their Dedicated cluster since 08:10 UTC, complaining about both latency and unexpected billing spikes. They say the errors started after enabling long_context for a few routes.
leah_sre: Copy. Any repro steps from the customer?
samir_eng: Customer provided a curl replay and timestamps. Looks like long context requests (60k tokens) then lots of short requests — KV cache eviction rate jumps.
maria_oncall: Pasting the short log they sent:```
2026-02-15T08:09:58Z INFO request id=abc123 route=/generate tokens=59821 result=ok
2026-02-15T08:10:04Z WARN eviction rate=0.78 pressure=high tenant=ledgex
2026-02-15T08:10:05Z ERROR serve 429 tenant=ledgex reason=throttle_kv_cache
```
eve_support: They also attached a billing alert screenshot showing token usage spike and an invoice flag. They've requested a credit and a root cause.
leah_sre: Quick triage results from our side: cluster-host: dcap-34 shows frequent KV cache GC loops and fragmented mem allocs. GPU mem is ok but host mem churn + page-faults cause process stalls which our router treats as degraded capacity => throttles to meet SLOs.
samir_eng: Relevant metrics: kv_evictions/sec spikes to ~650, kv_fragmentation_ratio=0.44, long_context_count rises, autoscaler did not add nodes because aggregated p99 latency stayed under scale threshold but thrashing caused transient CPU stalls.
maria_oncall: So autoscaler conditions didn't account for KV eviction pressure. That explains no new capacity even while throughput dropped.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20260215-091. Paging eng-runtime.
jordan_billing: I can pre-approve a partial credit once we confirm the throttling window and confirm they were charged for retried tokens. Need exact window.
eve_support: Repro steps customer gave: 1) enable long_context=true for route x. 2) fire 4 concurrent requests with 50-60k tokens each. 3) replay many small 4-token requests from different clients. They say failures start ~90s after.
samir_eng: I reproduced locally on a smaller dev pool. Steps I ran:```bash
# replay long ctx
python replay.py --file ledgex_longctx.json --concurrency 4
# then burst small requests
wrk -t4 -c250 --latency http://dedicated.svc/route-x -d30s
```
Result: KV eviction waterfall then 429s from router with message "throttle_kv_cache".
leah_sre: Collected kernel logs and allocator traces: fragmentation shows many small free regions due to repeated alloc/free of large KV chunks. Also saw retries from model-worker processes increasing socket backlog.
maria_oncall: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily bump tenant KV quota for Ledgex on that pool (gives them breathing room) 2) enable aggressive prefix caching for their high-frequency routes 3) throttle long-context max size via tenant policy 4) schedule a hotfix to autoscaler to include kv_eviction_rate as a scaling signal. Which do we want now?
jordan_billing: We should offer a service credit for the throttled window and reimburse retry tokens. I'll queue the request once you confirm timestamps.
samir_eng: Quick patch we can roll now: change eviction-policy from lru to size-tiered on affected nodes — reduces fragmentation. It's low risk and reversible. I'll stage to canary nodes in 15m.
eve_support: Please also collect a list of affected requests sample ids for billing reconciliation. Customer said 08:09:45–08:14:00 UTC is the worst window.
leah_sre: Action log: - samir to push canary eviction-policy change (ETA 15m) - maria to add tenant throttle to cap long_context on route x (ETA 10m) - jordan to approve provisional credit (needs affected IDs) - eve to coordinate with customer and get replay artifacts.
ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime/evict-policy-canary -> dcap-34 (task id: 9f3b)
samir_eng: Canary shows eviction/sec down 60% and fragmentation_ratio -> 0.21. Router 429s dropped after ~45s post patch.
maria_oncall: Bumped tenant KV quota for Ledgex temporarily. Also added policy: max_long_context_tokens=32000 for route-x while we investigate.
eve_support: Customer acknowledges fewer 429s now and reduced latency. They're still asking about why billing jumped.
jordan_billing: Received affected request ids from eve. Credits drafted, will send approval notes.
samir_eng: Root cause summary for postmortem draft: - Customer workload mixes heavy long-context requests with bursty small requests. - Long-context writes and evictions create host memory fragmentation and allocator thrash. - Fragmentation + socket stalls cause router to classify node as degraded -> throttles tenant. - Autoscaler didn't trigger because p99 latency metric alone missed eviction-driven capacity loss.
leah_sre: Follow-ups: - Add kv_eviction_rate and fragmentation_ratio to autoscaler policy (P1) - Add tenant-level long_context caps and guardrails in Console (P1) - Improve allocator compaction for KV store (P2) - Billing: automated detection to exclude throttled retries from charge (P2)
eve_support: I'll propose these to customer and share ETA. Thanks for fast patching. :thumbsup:
samir_eng: Filing RFC for autoscaler signal change and small allocator compaction PR in next 48h.
maria_oncall: Marking incident resolved for now. Will monitor dcap-34 for 24h.
ops-bot: Incident INC-20260215-091 status -> resolved.
leah_sre: Will include metrics and plots in the postmortem.
